items.title: Why Royal Caribbean (RCL) Stock Is Down Today
items.summary: Shares of cruise vacation company Royal Caribbean (NYSE:RCL) fell 3.9% in the afternoon session after the company said it will buy half of Sandals and Beaches Resorts for about $3 billion. Royal Caribbean said the price is about 10 times forward EBITDA. Morgan Stanley has committed the debt to fund it. items.title: Should You Buy Carnival Stock While Europe Sails Emptier?
items.summary: Carnival Corporation (CCL) trades near $22, down about 26% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained close to 18%. The easy read on a cruise line that cheap is that demand finally cracked. It has not. Carnival lowered its 2026 yield outlook after the Middle East conflict hit its European sailings, and part of that cut was its own choice to protect price rather than fill cabins.

items.title: Palantir, IonQ, Royal Caribbean, Paychex, McDonald’s, and More Stocks That Explain Today’s Market
items.summary: Stocks fell Wednesday as investors faced uncertainty with the lack of positive news on the war in Iran and as oil prices moved higher.  IonQ  gained 6.6% after the company said its latest quantum computer, Superion 256, will be the first system in  Nvidia’s   quantum research center.  The new device will act as a specialized co-processor alongside an Nvidia GPU cluster.
